tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: This README explains the two-tier CA hierarchy: an offline Root CA that signs an Intermediate CA, and an online Issuing CA that issues end-entity certificates.

tour.title: Root CA Playbook
tour.description: The Root CA playbook creates the Root CA, generates the Intermediate CA key and CSR, signs it, and exports public artifacts.

tour.title: Root CA Role
tour.description: The root_ca role generates the encrypted Root CA private key and self-signed certificate on the offline host.

tour.title: Intermediate CA Role
tour.description: The intermediate_ca role generates the Issuing CA key, creates a CSR, and signs it with the Root CA — all on the offline host.

tour.title: Export Artifacts
tour.description: The export_artifacts role stages the public certificates (root, issuing, chain) and fetches them to root-ca/artifacts/ on the control node.

tour.title: Issuing CA Playbook
tour.description: The Issuing CA playbook imports those artifacts and deploys the online CA server with full system hardening.

tour.title: Issuing CA Role
tour.description: The issuing_ca role is the core — it imports the CA artifacts, sets up the OpenSSL CA database, and validates the trust chain.

tour.title: Certificate Profiles
tour.description: Certificate issuance is manual/privileged. The role deploys 4 certificate profile templates (server, client, infra, VPN) with appropriate OpenSSL extensions.

tour.title: CRL Management
tour.description: CRLs are generated via a deployed script and published to /var/www/html/crl/. A daily cron job auto-renews the CRL.

tour.title: OCSP Responder
tour.description: OCSP provides real-time revocation status as an alternative to CRLs. Optional — disabled by default. Runs as a dedicated non-root user.

tour.title: System Hardening
tour.description: The server is hardened with UFW firewall (deny all inbound, allow SSH/HTTPS/HTTP), Fail2Ban SSH protection, and locked-down SSH key access.
